hypothesis: Allocating bounded generation time to every variable row and using smaller mixed local/uniform pools will let reversible DFS reach beyond the four-row greedy depth, isolating search-policy effects from pool-starvation effects.
rationale: The prior pool experiment never reached DFS because row 0 consumed the full deadline seeking an infeasible pool size; per-row caps are a direct correction with no change to the frozen DTS contract.
expected_information_gain: Measures all four variable-row pool sizes, DFS depth and nodes, and whether any complete assignment survives independent validation.
method: Use the same fixed rows 2,3,5 and variable rows 0,1,4,6, with radius 25, but cap each pool at 250 unique masks, 5 seconds and 100000 attempts; then backtrack over the resulting pools for the remaining seed budget.
metric: variable-row compatible pool sizes, deepest disjoint assignment, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: Only a validator-accepted seven-row assignment is exact target progress; pool and DFS depth are diagnostic proxies.
kill_condition: Stop after three 30-second seeded runs or immediately on an independently validated target witness.
interpretation: The corrected per-row pool budget prevented the previous starvation pattern, but all three seeds found only a single compatible variable-row assignment and no disjoint pair. This is Level 1 negative search evidence, not a mathematical infeasibility result.
what_was_learned: Per-row caps allowed every pool to be generated and DFS to run, but the sampled pools were too mutually incompatible to reach depth two; broader sampling or a different exact representation is required.
recommended_next_action: Use a materially different exact formulation or representation; do not repeat the same sampled-pool configuration.
repetition_justification: This repeats the pool/backtracking method only with a new budget-allocation hypothesis directly motivated by the prior recorded starvation failure.
